title: DNS: How Domain Names Get Resolved

scenes.line1: Why does DNS break so often?
scenes.say: Why does DNS break so often? Let's see what really happens when you look up a domain name.
Your resolver asks a root server, then the top-level domain server, then the authoritative server for the domain. The answer is cached for the record's time to live, or TTL.

scenes.label: A, CNAME
scenes.sub: A maps name to IPv4. CNAME is an alias.
scenes.say: Common DNS records: A maps a name to an I-P-v-4 address. CNAME is just an alias for another name.

scenes.title: dig app.example.com
scenes.say: Test DNS with dig. Use plus trace to see the full lookup path, or dash x for reverse lookups.

scenes.question: What does TTL control in DNS?
scenes.wrong: How long a server is online
scenes.right: How long a DNS answer is cached
scenes.say: Interview trap: What does TTL control in DNS? It's not server uptime. TTL sets how long a DNS answer is cached.
